content.text: {"title":"The Kite That Carried Three Kinds of News","premise":"In a sunny kite workshop, Pip the young dragon wants a kite to carry a tiny message, while Nia wants to build one that will fly beautifully and safely. A spool of blue thread, a bright paper kite, a feather, and one sealed message make a small world where choices change both the flight and what the message means.","cast_and_props":"Characters: Pip, a young dragon who wants his message to reach Aunt Ember and is eager to do daring things; Nia, a careful child who wants a graceful, reliable kite and initially believes Pip's message is ordinary; Aunt Ember, an unseen recipient represented by her named mailbox and later by her reply flag. Props: kite, blue thread, red ribbon, feather, sealed message, workshop table, mailbox. Shared setting: Nia's kite workshop beside a breezy hill. Keep the active entities to pip, nia, ember, kite, thread, ribbon, feather, message, mailbox.","kernels_and_interactions":"Use four kernel families: (1) assembly and decoration: attach thread, choose tail material, place feather, seal or open the message pocket; (2) observation and telling: Nia observes the message mark or wind flag, then tells Pip what she learned; this knowledge enables a later choice; (3) transfer and invitation: ownership of the kite or message can change, and Pip can invite Nia to fly together; (4) performance and delivery: launch the kite, let it carry the message, and record whether Aunt Ember receives it. Distinct problems arise from seeds: A) Nia's initial safe-material preference conflicts with Pip's desire for a spectacular red-ribbon tail; the heavy tail makes a slow, low flight, so they must trade decoration for lift or accept a different delivery; B) Pip believes the feather mark means Aunt Ember wants a dragon drawing, while Nia discovers it is Aunt Ember's request for a weather note; their mistaken beliefs produce a rewritten message and a thoughtful, useful delivery; C) Pip thinks Aunt Ember expects a private message, but Nia learns the mailbox is beside a children's kite gathering; they must choose a public sky-message, yielding shared performance rather than secret delivery. The same observation, discussion, construction, and launch scenes can appear in all three paths, but their conditions and effects differ.","seed_parameters":"Seed 1764253553 (index 4) should deterministically choose 2–4 initial facts: kite.tail_material in {none, ribbon, feather}; message.mark in {dragon, weather, gathering}; mailbox.audience in {private, public}; pip.knows.message_purpose in {None, dragon_drawing, weather_note, private_note}; nia.safe_preference in {thread, feather}; and initial ownership of kite/message. Use seed variation to alter what is wanted, believed, traded, made, or performed—not merely wording. Declare every slot before use, including kite.tail_material, kite.airborne, kite.carrying, kite.owner, message.text_kind, message.delivered, mailbox.audience, mailbox.reply, pip.knows.message_purpose, nia.knows.message_purpose, nia.agrees.public_flight, and pip.content.","candidate_scenes":"Offer 16–18 candidates: inspect_message (observe mark; prerequisite for informed choices); inspect_wind (observe wind flag; enables tail choice); ask_about_message (tell Nia the message purpose when Pip knows it); compare_tails (Nia and Pip discuss thread, ribbon, and feather); choose_thread; choose_ribbon; choose_feather; attach_tail; tuck_message; retie_tail (only if the chosen tail is unsuitable, not a repair loop); explain_audience (tell public/private fact); invite_shared_flight (pivotal, sets agreement); hand_kite_to_pip (transfer); walk_to_hill; launch_kite (sets airborne); perform_sky_message (sets kite.carrying and message.delivered, only after the appropriate agreement); read_reply (observe mailbox.reply); celebrate_flight. Reuse inspect_message, compare_tails, attach_tail, tuck_message, launch_kite, and celebrate_flight across materially different paths. Aim for 5–10 selected events, with only invite_shared_flight and one belief-turn marked pivotal.","constraints":"Goal may be pip.content == True, but require concrete outcome keys: message.delivered, kite.tail_material, mailbox.reply, and nia.agrees.public_flight. Use premise_keys kite.tail_material, message.mark, mailbox.audience, and nia.safe_preference; outcome_keys message.delivered, kite.tail_material, and mailbox.reply. Every action requiring knowledge must be guarded by the relevant knows slot; no mind reading. A launch requires a selected tail, attached tail, tucked message, and either private delivery or public-flight agreement. A ribbon path must not claim a high flight if the simulated weight makes it low. Do not invent a recipient's appearance: Aunt Ember's reply is represented by mailbox.reply. Keep all state scalar and entity-prefixed. Use observe/tell/transfer at least twice where they enable later actions. Use conditional scene cards so prose names the actual tail, audience, belief, and reply.","different_endings":"Ending A—graceful private delivery: the feather-tail kite rises quietly, the message reaches Aunt Ember's private mailbox, and her small green reply flag lifts; final image: the feather trembles above the hill like a tiny bird waving. Ending B—useful weather delivery: after Pip changes the message from a dragon drawing to a weather note, the kite arrives low but safely; Aunt Ember sends back a silver sun symbol, and Nia smiles at the kite's honest wobble. Ending C—public sky performance: the red ribbon makes a grand, low swoop over the children's gathering; the message becomes a cheer or drawing shared by everyone, and the ribbon curls around the blue thread like a dancing dragon. Provide two complete prose variants for each ending, guarded by the actual final slots, with no moral explanation."}
